title: Least-lexicographic graded initial ideal of a polynomial ideal
statement: Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\ge0$, and put $P=L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For any ideal $H\subseteq P$, define $\operatorname{in}_{\min}^{\mathrm{gr}}(H)$ to be the ideal generated by the monomials $T^\alpha$ for which there is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $p\in H$ with $\alpha$ the lexicographically least exponent in its support, comparing $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ in that order. Homogeneous means that all monomials in the support have one common total degree. The zero polynomial contributes no generator; each generating monomial has coefficient $1$. For homogeneous $H$, this is the fixed-degree least-monomial initial ideal used in the generic-coordinate statement.

source.place: Graded initial ideal in the generic-coordinate input recalled in Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8 and before Theorem 9.6, printed pp.273 and 278; the explicit least fixed-degree lexicographic convention and the ideal generated by homogeneous least monomials are specified in lem-trf-graded-generic-initial-borel, statement and proof step 3. ILO VIII 2.3.13, p.94 is resolution context only; supporting BM and Bayer--Stillman papers are not locally available.
